players.product: MEMS timing (clocks/oscillators) for AI servers & optical modules

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 revenue was $157.4 million, up 127% year-over-year and 39% sequentially; gross margin 67.1% (up 8.9 points), operating margin 34% versus 10% a year ago, and non-GAAP EPS $2.34, up 400%; every business unit and every region grew more than 50%, some over 100%.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $157.4 million, +127% YoY, +39% QoQ; gross margin 67.1%; operating margin 34%

quarterly_data.signal: Communications, Enterprise and Data Center (CED) revenue was $101.2 million, up 181% year-over-year and 34% sequentially, crossing $100 million in quarterly revenue for the ninth consecutive quarter of triple-digit growth, reflecting demand for precision timing across AI infrastructure including optical modules, switches, accelerators and related high-performance systems; CED is expected to post triple-digit growth again in Q3.

First growth driver is bandwidth: the move to 1.6T optical modules; in 2027 SiTime expects its 1.6T revenue to grow by 100% while 800G also grows significantly, in applications expected to be a combined $450 million of SAM in 2027 where SiTime has significant market share — share and ASPs are significantly higher on 1.6T than 800G because these modules need higher frequencies and performance.

Second driver is further adoption of synchronization by hyperscalers across both compute and networking nodes, increasing demand for the Elite family of Super-TCXOs and adding several hundred dollars of content per data center rack, with density rising as accurate clocks are needed across GPUs, TPUs, CPUs, switches and accelerator cards; third driver is AI data center spending beyond traditional hyperscalers — new OEMs and ODMs, enterprise, captive, neocloud and sovereign data centers.
quarterly_data.figure: several hundred dollars of timing content per data center rack

quarterly_data.signal: Book-to-bill, order size and ASPs all grew on a higher-value product mix; many customers are now placing orders 12 to 18 months in advance, so visibility into 2027 keeps improving; channel inventory held at tight target levels reflecting strong pull-through; inventory increased to $103.9 million to support Q3 demand.
quarterly_data.figure: orders placed 12 to 18 months in advance; inventory $103.9 million

quarterly_data.signal: Closed the acquisition of Renesas' Timing Products Division (TPD — FemtoClock, VersaClock, and buffers of over $100 million in revenue) on July 1: 10,000 customers, 70% gross margins and nearly 70% of revenue from CED; the prior guidance of $300 million revenue in the 12 months post-close is now expected to be exceeded, though the business is supply-constrained during the Renesas transition services period; funded with $1.35 billion of zero-coupon convertible senior notes due 2031.
quarterly_data.figure: TPD: 10,000 customers, 70% gross margin, ~70% CED; $300 million 12-month revenue target to be exceeded

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 revenue guided to $285 million-$295 million: SiTime excluding TPD at $200 million-$210 million (up 30% sequentially at the midpoint, a step change reflecting backlog strength and customer demand forecasts particularly in CED) plus approximately $85 million from TPD; combined gross margin approximately 68% ±1 point, operating expenses $80 million-$85 million, and non-GAAP EPS $3.50-$3.65.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue $285 million-$295 million; core SiTime $200 million-$210 million (+30% QoQ); TPD ~$85 million

quarterly_data.signal: Management reiterates a multi-year growth rate of 30% or a little higher and sees no signs of slowdown in 2027 (AI also lifts TPD, whose business is 70% data center and other AI); timing is moving from a discrete component to integration through chiplets, advanced substrates and modules, which SiTime expects to expand its CED SAM by $2.5 billion by 2030 in opportunities that do not exist today, and the acquisition accelerates the path to $1 billion in revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: multi-year growth ~30%; CED SAM +$2.5 billion by 2030
